title: The light in my allotment shed was on 🔦

hook_text: At 4:36 in the morning the light in my allotment shed was on, and I live alone on the hill.

scenes.narration: At 4:36 in the morning the light in my allotment shed was on, and I live alone on the hill.
I saw it from my kitchen window, a small yellow square among the dark bean rows. I keep the key on a nail inside the house. The padlock was fine.
I walked down the path in my wellies. The grass was soaked. The light had a faint orange flicker, like a paraffin lamp, and I smelled hot tea.
I put my eye to the gap in the door. Inside, a table was laid for two. Two cups, steaming. A chair pulled out. A coat on the hook, my father's coat.
My father died the winter before last. This was his shed. I had not opened it since the day of the funeral, not once, not even to tidy.
I rattled the padlock, and the door swung open on its own. The room was warm. The tea was fresh. And one of the cups had my name on it.
I stood there a long time. Then I noticed a newspaper by the cups, folded to the crossword. Last week's date. And all the clues filled in by hand.
The writing was mine. I do not remember writing it. A voice behind me said, quietly, kettle's boiled, lad, sit down, and I felt a hand on my shoulder.
So tell me. Do you sit down, or run up the hill?
